lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Zechariah: overview
nodes.d: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?
ev: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)

nodes.t: Turn unto me, and I will turn unto you
nodes.d: In the second year of Darius the LORD tells Zechariah to say that he was sore displeased with the fathers, who did not heed the former prophets, and calls the people to turn to him so that he will turn to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the invitation in Zechariah 1:3 and why the fathers are mentioned?
ev: Read the call of 1:3
Say what the fathers did when the prophets spoke (1:4-6)

nodes.t: The riders among the myrtle trees
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a night vision of riders sent through the earth; the angel of the LORD asks how long the LORD will withhold mercy from Jerusalem, and the LORD answers with comfort that he is jealous for Zion, will return with mercies, and his house will be built.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD asks in Zechariah 1:12 and how the LORD replies?
ev: Describe the vision and the angel's question (1:8-12)
Describe the LORD's answer (1:13-17)

nodes.t: Four horns and four carpenters
nodes.d: Zechariah sees four horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem, and four carpenters who come to terrify them and cast out the horns of the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vision of the four horns and the four carpenters?
ev: Say what the horns are explained to be (1:19, 1:21)
Say what the carpenters come to do (1:21)

nodes.t: The man with the measuring line
nodes.d: A man goes to measure Jerusalem, but an angel says it will be inhabited like towns without walls, for the LORD will be a wall of fire and the glory in her midst; exiles are called to flee Babylon, and many nations will be joined to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Jerusalem's walls in Zechariah 2:4-5?
ev: Describe the vision and the message about walls (2:1-5)
Say what the LORD promises in 2:10-11

nodes.t: Joshua the high priest cleansed
nodes.d: Joshua the high priest stands in filthy garments before the angel of the LORD with Satan accusing; the LORD rebukes Satan, has the filthy clothes removed, says he has caused Joshua's iniquity to pass, and promises his servant the Branch and the removal of the land's iniquity in one day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the vision of Joshua in filthy garments and what the LORD does for him?
ev: Retell what happens to Joshua's clothing (3:3-5)
Say what the LORD says about the Branch and 'one day' (3:8-9)

nodes.t: The lampstand and the two olive trees
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a gold lampstand with two olive trees; the LORD tells Zerubbabel that it is not by might nor power but by his spirit, that Zerubbabel who laid the foundation will finish the house, and that none should despise the day of small things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Zerubbabel in Zechariah 4:6 and 4:9-10?
ev: Read 4:6 and say whom it is spoken to
Say what Zerubbabel's hands do (4:9)
Describe the two olive trees (4:14)

nodes.t: The flying roll and the woman in the ephah
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a flying scroll that is a curse on thieves and false swearers, and an ephah in which a woman called wickedness is shut with lead and carried by two women with wings to the land of Shinar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two visions of Zechariah 5 and what each is said to mean?
ev: Say what the flying roll is and whom it enters (5:3-4)
Say what the woman in the ephah is called and where the ephah goes (5:8, 5:11)

nodes.t: Four chariots; crowns for Joshua; the Branch
nodes.d: Four chariots come out from between two bronze mountains as spirits of the heavens going throughout the earth; then Zechariah is told to make crowns and set them on Joshua the high priest, speaking of a man called the Branch who will build the temple and rule.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Zechariah is told to do with the crown and what is said about the Branch?
ev: Describe the vision of the chariots (6:1-8)
Describe the crown action and what it says of the Branch (6:11-13)

nodes.t: Fasting question: did ye fast unto me?
nodes.d: Messengers ask whether the people should continue the fast of the fifth month; the LORD asks whether they fasted for him and tells them to render true judgment and mercy, since the fathers hardened their hearts against the law and were scattered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says in Zechariah 7:9-10 in answer to the question about fasting?
ev: State the question that is asked (7:3)
Read the commands of 7:9-10
Say what happened because the fathers would not hear (7:11-14)

nodes.t: The LORD returns to dwell in Jerusalem
nodes.d: The LORD says he has returned to Zion and Jerusalem will be a city of truth with old people and playing children in her streets; he will save his people, make them a blessing, and tells them to speak truth and judge truly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Zechariah 8:1-17 pictures Jerusalem when the LORD returns?
ev: Describe the picture of 8:4-5
Read the promise of 8:8
List the commands of 8:16-17

nodes.t: Fasts become feasts; nations seek the LORD
nodes.d: The LORD says the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become joy and cheerful feasts, and many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the LORD, with ten men from all languages taking hold of a Jew.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD answers the fasting question and what the nations will do?
ev: Name the fasts that become feasts (8:19)
Describe what the peoples say and do (8:20-23)

nodes.t: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding on an ass
nodes.d: A burden against Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre and Philistia is followed by a call for Zion to rejoice because her just and saving King comes lowly on an ass; he cuts off chariot and bow, speaks peace to the nations, and the LORD saves his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the King of Zechariah 9:9-10 and what he does?
ev: Say what is said of the King in 9:9
Describe his rule in 9:10
Read the promise to prisoners in 9:11-12

nodes.t: The LORD visits his flock
nodes.d: The LORD tells his people to ask him for rain, rejects idols and false shepherds, and promises to strengthen Judah and Joseph, gather and bring them back, and make them strong in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promises his flock in Zechariah 10 and what he says about idols and shepherds?
ev: Say what Israel is told to ask (10:1)
Say what the LORD says of the shepherds and flock (10:2-3)
Describe the regathering (10:8-10)

nodes.t: Two staves and thirty pieces of silver
nodes.d: Zechariah is told to shepherd the flock of the slaughter and takes two staves called Beauty and Bands; the flock rejects him, he breaks the staves, is paid thirty pieces of silver which the LORD tells him to cast to the potter, and a foolish shepherd is announced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Zechariah does with the two staves and the thirty pieces of silver?
ev: Name the two staves and what breaking each means (11:10, 11:14)
Retell what happens to the thirty pieces of silver (11:12-13)

nodes.t: Jerusalem a burdensome stone; they look on the pierced
nodes.d: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone to the nations that gather against her, and will pour on David's house and Jerusalem the spirit of grace and supplications, so that they look on him whom they have pierced and mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Zechariah 12:10 says the LORD will pour out and what the people do?
ev: Describe what happens to nations that attack Jerusalem (12:2-3, 12:9)
Read 12:10 and describe the mourning that follows (12:10-14)

nodes.t: A fountain opened; the shepherd smitten
nodes.d: In that day a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness and idols and false prophets are cut off; the LORD calls the sword against his shepherd, the sheep are scattered, and a third part is refined as silver and calls on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the fountain of Zechariah 13:1 and what the LORD says about the shepherd and the refined third in 13:7-9?
ev: Read 13:1
Say what the LORD calls the sword to do (13:7)
Describe the refining of the third part (13:9)

nodes.t: The day of the LORD: king over all the earth
nodes.d: The LORD gathers all nations against Jerusalem, then goes forth to fight, standing on the mount of Olives; living waters flow, he is king over all the earth, the survivors keep the feast of tabernacles, and everything is holiness to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Zechariah 14:9 says about the LORD and how the book ends?
ev: Describe the siege and the LORD's coming (14:2-5)
Read 14:9 and describe the closing picture (14:16-21)

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: Jesus enters Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for an ass and colt, and rides toward Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and branches and cry Hosanna to the son of David; Matthew says this fulfils a word about the King coming meek on an ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus came into Jerusalem and what the crowds said?
ev: Describe the entry
Say what the crowds shouted

nodes.t: Peter’s boast and Gethsemane
nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the disciples will scatter and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays three times that the cup may pass but not his will, while the disciples sleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell what Jesus prayed
Say what happened to the disciples in the garden

nodes.t: Judas repents and the field of blood
nodes.d: Seeing Jesus condemned, Judas returns the thirty silver pieces, confesses innocent blood and hangs himself; the priests buy the potter’s field, and Matthew links this to a word of Jeremy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Judas and the silver?
ev: Say what Judas did with the money
Say what the priests did with it

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: Peter’s boast and Gethsemane
nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the sheep will be scattered and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays “Abba, Father” that the cup might pass yet not his will, and finds the disciples asleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell Jesus’ prayer
Say what Peter said and what Jesus answered

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: The crowd takes palm branches and cries 'Hosanna', Jesus rides a young donkey as written, the disciples later remember this after he is glorified, and the Pharisees say the world has gone after him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry into Jerusalem in John?
ev: Say how the crowd greeted Jesus and what John says the disciples understood later.

nodes.t: His Side Pierced and the Burial
nodes.d: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs but pierce his side, and John says these things fulfil Scripture; Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus wrap his body with spices and lay it in a new tomb in a garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Jesus' body after his death and who buried him?
ev: Say what the soldiers did and who buried Jesus.

nodes.t: Ephesians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.t: Put off the old man, put on the new
nodes.d: Paul tells the Ephesians not to live as the Gentiles do but to put off the old man and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness, with specific commands about truth, anger, work, speech and forgiveness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to put off the old man and put on the new, using Ephesians 4:22-24 and one example from 4:25-32?
ev: Contrast the old and new man (4:22-24)
List specific commands in 4:25-32
Say what we are told not to grieve (4:30)

nodes.t: The temple measured and the two witnesses
nodes.d: John is told to measure the temple while the court is given to the Gentiles, and two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth, are killed by the beast from the pit, lie in the great city three and a half days, and are raised and called up to heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the two witnesses do and what happens to them in Revelation 11?
ev: Describe what John is told to measure and not measure
Describe the two witnesses and what happens to them
Say how the survivors respond in 11:13
